clue.text: Prim type whose terms of employment are instructive

definitions.text: Prim type whose terms of employment are instructive

parts.note: surface reading: a starchy, proper sort of person

parts.words: whose terms of employment are instructive
parts.note: setter's reading: her working terms are school terms, spent teaching

explanation.surface: A description of a buttoned-up person whose contract happens to be educational.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terms' are school terms, not contract conditions: the prim type works through the school year teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmarm is an old-fashioned, strict female teacher, a stock figure of primness.

clue.text: Old knight's joy, sheltering girl on island

indicators.note: to shelter something is to hold it inside, so the first word goes around what follows

parts.note: cheer is gladness, joy
Val is a girl's name, short for Valerie
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A knight of old takes pleasure in protecting a girl on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Chevalier is French for horseman, hence knight; the girl and island sit together inside the joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Chevalier is the French word for a knight, used in English for a mounted knight of old.

clue.text: Former description of silence after beheading

indicators.note: beheading cuts off the head, the first letter of the word described

parts.note: from the proverb that silence is golden

explanation.surface: An old account of the quiet after an execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speech is silver, silence is golden' supplies the description.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden means of former times, as in the olden days.

clue.text: Injured Latin hero — one displaying great courage

indicators.note: something injured is damaged out of its proper shape, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A wounded Roman hero still showing tremendous bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard I of England was called the Lionheart for his bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: A lionheart is a person of exceptional bravery, with the heart of a lion.

clue.text: Girl is able to set up yearbook

parts.note: Alma is a girl's name

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: can means is able

explanation.surface: A girl who knows how to put together a school yearbook.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is an annual publication listing calendar data and events of the year.

clue.text: Roughly drop note

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a tiny liquid measure, about a drop
second meaning: a musical note, the half note

explanation.surface: A command to discard a note carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly drop' looks like an instruction, but it is a definition: an apothecaries' minim is about one drop.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is a sixtieth of a fluid dram, roughly a drop, and also a musical half note.

clue.text: Sound reflection Eastern church provided old follower

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for Eastern
CH is the usual abbreviation for church
O is a common abbreviation for old
a second hint at the answer: one who repeats what another says, a mere imitator

explanation.surface: A description of how sound bounces around an Eastern church full of old faithful followers.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters come from E, CH and O; 'follower' adds a second sense of ECHO, someone who merely copies another.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is sound bounced back from a surface, heard again after the original noise.

clue.text: Record 22 docked in harbour

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to enter is to record, as in a ledger
the answer to 22 down

explanation.surface: Logging a ship that has docked in port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Docked' and 'harbour' both suggest ships, but one cuts a letter and the other is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbour and to entertain both mean to hold a thought or feeling in the mind.

clue.text: It can be played with devastating effect

definitions.text: It can be played with devastating effect

parts.note: surface reading: a game, piece of music or card
setter's reading: the thing in the idiom about causing chaos, which one plays

explanation.surface: A trump card or killer tune played to devastating effect.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'play havoc with' means to cause great disruption.
explanation.definitionFit: Havoc means widespread destruction, and the set phrase to play havoc is to wreck things.

clue.text: Principal opportunity for clearance

parts.note: the principal of a school is its head
room in the sense of scope or chance, as in room for improvement

explanation.surface: A headteacher sees a chance to get something cleared.
explanation.definitionFit: Headroom is the vertical space above, the clearance under a bridge or ceiling.

clue.text: Local inhabitant in bed at Whitstable?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone born in a place
second meaning: a farmed oyster lying in an oyster bed

explanation.surface: A resident of the Kent coast tucked up asleep in Whitstable.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitstable is a Kent seaside town famous for oysters; 'natives' is the name for its native oysters, grown in beds offshore.
explanation.definitionFit: A native is a person born in a place, and also a cultivated British oyster.

clue.text: Strike constraining a large corporation

indicators.note: to constrain is to hold something in, so the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: to strike with a fist
taken as written

explanation.surface: Industrial action holding back a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large corporation' looks like a business, but corporation is old humorous slang for a big belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is a jocular dated word for a pot belly, so a large one is a protruding stomach.

clue.text: Miners beginning to exhibit spirited strength in numbers

parts.note: the National Union of Mineworkers, Britain's miners' union

indicators.note: the beginning of the next word means only its opening letter is used

parts.note: first letter of the word
racy means lively, spirited

explanation.surface: Striking miners showing collective might: the old slogan of strength in numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUM was the National Union of Mineworkers, the union behind the 1984-85 British miners' strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Numeracy is skill or competence with arithmetic, a punning reading of the slogan about solidarity.

clue.text: Prejudice some exploit to get at Jack

definitions.text: some exploit to get at Jack
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the weighting of a bowl in lawn bowls, used to curve it towards the small target ball

explanation.surface: Someone's prejudice being used against a man called Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: In bowls, a game played on a lawn, the jack is the small white target ball; each bowl is weighted on one side so players can curl it in.
explanation.definitionFit: Bias is an unfair inclination for or against, and also the lopsided weighting of a bowl.

clue.text: Secondary argument from team put out

parts.note: a side is a team
to issue is to put out, publish

explanation.surface: A minor dispute arising from a team being knocked out.
explanation.definitionFit: A side issue is a subsidiary point or question, peripheral to the main matter.

clue.text: Recognition EC pace can't change

indicators.note: to change these letters is to alter their order into a new word

parts.note: the letters of these words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A complaint that the European Community's pace of change is fixed, so recognition never comes.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the European Community, the old name for what became the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: Acceptance and recognition both mean approval or acknowledgement of something as valid.

clue.text: Best prayer concocted when lacking a minister

indicators.note: something concocted is mixed up from ingredients, so the letters are stirred together
lacking means going without, so one letter is left out of the mix

parts.note: the letters of these words
the letter to remove

explanation.surface: A finely crafted prayer composed in the absence of a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A presbyter is an elder or priest in certain churches, a minister of religion.

clue.text: Cease trading with neighbouring county

parts.note: close means near, neighbouring
County Down, in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A firm stops doing business with the county next door.
explanation.walkthrough: Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To close down is to shut a business for good, ending all commercial activity.

clue.text: Praiseworthy volunteers in conceivable situation

indicators.note: the volunteers are placed inside, so the other word wraps around them
situation completes the phrase: the volunteers are situated within the other word

parts.note: credible means believable, conceivable
the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Volunteers deserve praise when they find themselves in a plausible situation.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve, a frequent crossword source of those two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Creditable means deserving credit or praise, a close synonym of praiseworthy.

clue.text: Serviceman's cap? Harte accepting one with thanks

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the writer's name wraps around what follows

parts.note: Bret Harte, the American writer of Wild West stories
Roman numeral one
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: A soldier's headgear, and the writer Harte taking one gratefully.
explanation.walkthrough: The serviceman is a priest who conducts church services, not a soldier; the question mark flags the twist. Harte stands for his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is the square cap worn by Roman Catholic clergy, who take services.

clue.text: Contradictory responses to request for recess

parts.note: one of the responses is a flat refusal
the reply contradicting that refusal is an agreement

explanation.surface: Mixed answers when someone asks for a break.
explanation.walkthrough: The two contradictory answers are a refusal followed by agreement, NO then OK.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a small recess or corner in a room.

clue.text: Paint remover — one producing bare finish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a solvent or tool for taking off old paint
second meaning: a performer whose act ends naked

explanation.surface: A decorating product that leaves woodwork bare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bare finish' reads as decorating jargon for unpainted wood, but also describes how an exotic dancer's act ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripper is both a chemical for removing paint and a striptease performer.

clue.text: It isn't commonly a corrupt condition

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the colloquial contraction of it is not
second meaning: a trace of contamination or moral stain

explanation.walkthrough: 'Commonly' marks a vulgar or dialect form: 'tain't is a colloquial contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A taint is a contaminating stain or corruption, and the dialect contraction spells the same.

clue.text: Galley of tried strength

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a galley is a printer's trial print for correction
second meaning: the tested alcoholic strength of spirits

explanation.surface: A ship's galley of proven sturdiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Galley' suggests a ship or kitchen, but it is printing jargon for a trial page.
explanation.definitionFit: A proof is a trial printing for correction, and proof is a standard measure of spirit strength.

clue.text: Refreshment counter providing punch

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bar serving food and drink
second meaning: a blow, to strike

explanation.surface: A snack bar that serves the drink punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punch' looks like the party drink served at the counter, but it is a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffet is a refreshment bar, and also a blow or to strike repeatedly.

clue.text: Managed football club without European money

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the club's letters go around the other word

parts.note: FC is the standard abbreviation for Football Club
ran means managed

explanation.surface: Someone ran a football club without any European funding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking, but in the old sense it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was the currency of France, Belgium and other European states, and still of Switzerland.

clue.text: Poem about race meeting mostly a failure

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the poem's title runs backwards

parts.note: If is Rudyard Kipling's famous poem

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Royal Ascot, the famous English horse-race meeting

explanation.surface: A poem about a race meeting that mostly flops.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a racecourse in Berkshire whose Royal Ascot meeting is a high point of the English social season.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is a complete, humiliating failure or debacle.

clue.text: Figure represented on target

indicators.note: something represented is presented again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A number shown being exactly on target.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetragon is a four-sided plane figure, a quadrilateral in geometry.

clue.text: Eyesore appearing in the middle of last year

indicators.note: the answer shows up in the centre of the following words, straddling their join

parts.note: taken from inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Something ugly showing up in the middle of last year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eyesore' is read literally: a sore on the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, literally a sore eye.

clue.text: Accommodation going fast — no hurdles to cross here

parts.note: a flat is a home, a place of accommodation
racing means moving at speed

explanation.surface: Somewhere to live sells quickly, with no obstacles in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Flat racing is horse racing without jumps, as opposed to hurdles and steeplechases.
explanation.definitionFit: In flat racing horses run on level courses with no jumps or fences, unlike National Hunt racing.
